acceptance: Global core.hooksPath hooks do not fire during store init even on Git 2.28-2.30, or the declared minimum Git version is raised to 2.31.
A test verifies hook suppression across supported Git versions.
context:
Discovered during store init isolation testing (test_inherited_git_environment_and_global_hooks_are_ignored). GIT_CONFIG_COUNT requires Git >= 2.31.

Fixed in 1.3.1 by the first option (raise the minimum). PR #81 (merge a84cbe1, commit 5cb2871), release PR #82 (merge b4ebe03), tag v1.3.1, publish run https://github.com/joeharris76/tractable/actions/runs/44541687536. MIN_GIT_VERSION is now (2, 31) in git_store.py, so Store.open() refuses to create a store on git 2.28-2.30 with 'git 2.31 or newer is required' before any git init runs; the now-unconditional --no-write-fetch-head replaces the 2.29 check; README and CHANGELOG state the new minimum. Tests: tests/test_git_store.py::test_store_creation_refuses_git_below_the_minimum (faked 2.30.9 refused, minimum is 2.31) plus the existing test_inherited_git_environment_and_global_hooks_are_ignored, which exercises hook suppression on the supported git (a real run across git versions is not possible in one environment; below 2.31 is refused by version check). CI green.
description: git init fires global core.hooksPath hooks before the repository's local config can be written. open() sets GIT_CONFIG_COUNT / GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.hooksPath to /dev/null in the environment to isolate the init command, but GIT_CONFIG_COUNT requires Git >= 2.31. On Git 2.28 to 2.30, an installed global reference-transaction hook will still fire during git init. Either raise the minimum Git version to 2.31 or initialize stores with a template directory that disables hooks.
